heading: Languages Yon runs
body:
Yon supports JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Java, Groovy, C#, F#, Kotlin, PHP, Rust, Dart, Go and Ruby directly. Each controller can also use provider annotations (annotations on the classes that other classes need). Tachyon turns all annotations into plain code before the route runs. Tachyon starts each process and adapts the protocol. You need no annotation package at run time. To call a class in another of these languages, declare a `@Gateway` method. To reach other programs, call `relay(command, request)` yourself, or name the program in a `@Gateway` command.

Groovy (ADR 0072) writes the annotations as Java does: `@RequestRoute('/orders')`, `@GetRoute`, `@Service`, `@Needs`. Tachyon reads Groovy with the Java rules, and a semicolon at the end of a line is optional. Every field and method has a declared type, such as `String name` or `List<Order> findOrders()`; a member declared with `def` stops the build (TY1334), and a local variable inside a method may still use `def`. A model is a record, an enum or a class with typed fields, and code reads it with `import models.Order`. Groovy uses the Java protocol runtime, so the request is `HttpExchange` and `Yon.relay(command, exchange)` works as in Java. Tachyon compiles your Groovy together with that Java runtime (joint compilation) into one jar with the Groovy core library and runs it on the JDK. Tachyon finds Groovy 4 or newer through `GROOVY_HOME` or `groovyc` on `PATH`. Two Groovy rules matter for Tachyon code: `1.5` is a `BigDecimal`, so write `1.5d` for a `double`, and a closure that you put into a map needs its type, such as `{ request, execution -> ... } as Behaviors.HttpAdapter`.

F# (ADR 0073) writes the annotations as F# attributes, each on its own line: `[<RequestRoute("/orders")>]`, `[<GetRoute>]`, `[<Service>]`. A type takes the roles it needs as the parameters of its primary constructor, `type OrderService(orderStore: OrderStore) =`, the way Spring injects a class with one constructor, so F# needs no `Needs` attribute. Members that Tachyon reads write their types, for example `member this.GetOrder(id: int64) : Order =`. A model is an F# record, and code reads it with `open Models`. An F# file holds one type and no `module` or `namespace` line, and it has no file-level `let` (TY1335). F# runs on .NET with the same protocol runtime as C#, so F# code uses `Yon.Relay`, `DataSource`, `HttpRequestMessage` and `HttpResponseMessage` as C# does. Behavior annotations, events, lifecycle hooks, sockets and streams are not available in F# yet; Tachyon refuses them by name.
